genxml.title: WD33C93/WD33C93A SCSI bus interface controller as wired on the Indigo (R3000 and R4000 boards)
genxml.doc: The SCSI controller behind the Indigo's HPC1. The CPU reaches it through two byte ports in the HPC1 window: an address port, which on a read returns the auxiliary status register, and a data port. A write to the address port selects one of the chip's internal registers; each access to the data port reads or writes the selected register and then advances the selection by one, except for the data and command registers, which stay selected. The internal registers are described in the chip's own index space (offsets are the value written to the address port); the two ports are in two port spaces whose offsets are bytes from the HPC1 window base, physical 0x1fb80000, big-endian view. Names and layouts follow the Western Digital data sheet and the public NetBSD driver, with the IRIX driver's own names only where the page says so. Grades: established means read in full from the IRIX R4000 Indigo SCSI driver object, the 4.0.5D PROM or the data sheet; inferred means a reasoned reading; unknown means nothing shipped settles it. Reset values are from the data sheet, so they hold for the part. Nothing was measured on a board. The prose is in devices/wd33c93/README.md.

struct.name: OWN_ID
struct.doc: Own ID and CDB size. The bus ID in bits 2:0 and the configuration bits are sampled by the Reset command, so they take effect only after a reset. Both the PROM and IRIX write it before every Reset. In advanced mode, bits 3:0 hold the CDB length for a command group the chip does not know (the driver writes it from startwd93 only on parts that answered the reset with advanced features). Bit 5 is EIH on rev E/F A parts and RAF on the B. A qtest can discriminate: write 0 to 7 and read each back; the presence test needs all eight bits to read back.

struct.name: CONTROL
struct.doc: Control. Interrupt and DMA mode selection. IRIX and the PROM write 0x2d (burst DMA mode) once the chip has been reset and detected as a WD33C93A or B, and 0x8d (single-byte DMA mode) when the burst flag is clear or the chip answered the reset with status 0. A qtest can discriminate: reset clears it; write 0x2d and read it back.

struct.name: TIMEOUT
struct.doc: Selection timeout. Zero disables the timeout. IRIX writes 0x40; the PROM writes 0x40 through a helper called at the end of its reset routine. During the hinv bus scan IRIX divides the value by 32 (rounded up) and later restores it, to shorten selects of missing targets. A qtest can discriminate: a Select to a target that is not present stays pending when this is zero, and ends with status 0x42 when it is not.

struct.name: CDB
struct.doc: CDB bytes 1 to 12 for Select-and-Transfer. The same offsets are total sectors, heads, cylinders, logical address and head and cylinder numbers for Translate Address. The 12 bytes are written with one address-port write of 3 and as many data-port writes as the CDB has bytes, using the auto-increment (IRIX stops at 12, rounding a 13+ byte count down). On a WD33C93B with RAF set, index 3 reads back a revision code after Reset (below). A qtest can discriminate: auto-increment and cdb1 reading zero after reset.

struct.name: TARGET_LUN
struct.doc: Target LUN. The initiator writes the LUN for the Identify message; after Select-and-Transfer completes it holds the target's status byte (IRIX reads it on status 0x16 and stores it as the SCSI status). During reselection with advanced features it holds the Identify byte (TLV in bit 7, DOK in bit 6). IRIX reads it first in the interrupt handler and then reads the command phase register by letting the address auto-increment.

struct.name: COMMAND_PHASE
struct.doc: Command phase: how far a Select-and-Transfer has progressed. The chip advances it as phases complete (CPH_ constants); the driver writes a value back and reissues Select-and-Transfer to resume. IRIX writes 0x00 to start, 0x41 after Save Data Pointers, 0x44 after reselection and 0x45 after the Identify message or a parity error. A qtest can discriminate: after Select-and-Transfer to a missing target it reads 0x00; to a present one 0x10 and up.

struct.name: SYNC_TRANSFER
struct.doc: Synchronous transfer: offset in bits 3:0 (zero means asynchronous), period in bits 6:4 (0 is 8 clock cycles, 2 to 7 are that many cycles), bit 7 fast SCSI on the B. IRIX initialises the per-target copy to 0x20 (two cycles, offset zero, asynchronous) and loads the target's value before every command. The PROM reads it before the first reset and restores it afterwards (inferred: to keep a boot target's setting).

struct.name: TRANSFER_COUNT
struct.doc: 24-bit transfer count, most significant byte at index 12h, written with one address-port write of 12h and three data-port writes. IRIX writes zero for commands with no data phase and the HPC1-programmed length otherwise (at most 0xfffffc). After an interrupted transfer it holds the bytes not transferred (IRIX reads it back when it saves the data pointers). A qtest can discriminate: three-byte write through the auto-increment and read back.

struct.name: DEST_ID
struct.doc: Destination ID: target to select or reselect, bits 2:0; bit 6 DPD gives the expected data direction in advanced mode (1 is device to host); bit 7 SCC and bit 5 DF are target-mode chaining controls. IRIX writes the target ID with bit 6 from the data direction (the command's 0x40 flag) at every command start. The PROM's first-time path reads it back and saves bits 2:0.

struct.name: SOURCE_ID
struct.doc: Source ID: ER (bit 7) enables reselection, ES (bit 6) selection, DSP (bit 5) ignores select parity; bit 3 SIV and bits 2:0 report who selected or reselected the chip. IRIX and the PROM write 0x80 after a reset when disconnect is enabled (the PROM's per-controller enable word is 1) and 0 otherwise. After a reselect IRIX reads this register and then the SCSI status register by auto-increment and uses bits 2:0 to find the channel.

struct.name: SCSI_STATUS
struct.doc: SCSI status: the cause of the last interrupt, high nibble the group (0 reset, 1 done, 2 paused, 4 terminated, 8 service) and low nibble the qualifier or phase. Reading it clears INT in the auxiliary status register and the chip's interrupt request; the chip will not change it until it is read. The driver must not issue a command within 7 microseconds of reading it, or the chip ignores the command and sets LCI. Values acted on by IRIX are the STATUS_ constants. A qtest can discriminate: after Reset read 0x00 or 0x01 depending on own_id.eaf, then INT is clear.

struct.name: COMMAND
struct.doc: Command: bits 6:0 the command code, bit 7 single-byte transfer. The register stays selected after a write (no auto-increment). It must not be written while CIP or INT is set. A command written while an interrupt is pending is ignored and sets LCI; the IRIX driver handles that in wd93cmd_lci by reading SCSI status and rewriting the command. A qtest can discriminate: a write with INT set must leave LCI set and not start the command.

struct.name: DATA
struct.doc: Data register: the host side of the 12-byte FIFO. IRIX uses it in programmed-I/O message and inquiry phases, polling the DBR bit of the auxiliary status register, and never for bulk data. The register stays selected after an access. In the HPC1 burst mode the DMA channel moves bulk data through the same register without CPU involvement.

struct.name: QUEUE_TAG
struct.doc: Queue tag, WD33C93B only. IRIX never touches it. NetBSD writes 0x55 here and reads it back after a reset that returned status 0x01: if it reads 0x55 the part is a B, otherwise an A. On an A part the register does not exist and the read returns all ones (data sheet note 2 to the register map). A qtest can discriminate: the write sticks only on a model configured as a B.

struct.name: AUX_STATUS
struct.doc: Auxiliary status. Bit 7 INT is the interrupt-request pin: it stays set until the SCSI status register is read. Bit 6 LCI says a command was written while an interrupt was pending or the chip was busy decoding the last command, and the command was ignored. Bit 5 BSY is set while a level II command runs. Bit 4 CIP is set while the chip decodes a command; the command register may not be written while it is set. Bit 1 PE is a parity error, cleared when a new command is issued. Bit 0 DBR is data-buffer-ready for programmed data-register transfers. Both IRIX and the PROM poll bit 4 clear before every command and bit 7 for interrupts. A qtest can discriminate: after a hard reset read 0x80; after a Reset command and before the status read INT stays set; reading scsi_status clears bit 7.

struct.name: DATA_PORT
struct.doc: Data port. Reads and writes the internal register selected through the address port. Every IRIX and PROM access is a byte access. A qtest can discriminate: write own_id then read it back (the controller presence test, below).

struct.name: ADDRESS
struct.doc: Address port. A byte written here selects the internal register the next data-port access uses. No shipped code reads it back (a read returns the auxiliary status register). The index auto-increments after every data-port access except when the selected register is the data register or the command register. A qtest can discriminate: write 0x03, write three bytes to the data port, and read cdb1 to cdb3 back by writing 0x03 once and reading the data port three times.
